Isotonic Regression with 2d-grid-ordered isotonic constraints

solve_isotone_2d_grid.Rd

Isotonic Regression with 2d-grid-ordered isotonic constraints

Usage

solve_isotone_2d_grid(
  y,
  w = NULL,
  delta = 1,
  loss = "quadratic",
  eps = 1e-07,
  sol_ir = NULL
)

Arguments

y

data vector

w

weights (default is NULL)

delta

hyperparameter if method == "smoothH"

loss

type of loss wanted (either "quadratic" which is the isotonic regression or "smoothH" a smooth version of Huber loss)

eps

Numeric value greater than zero (default: 1e-7). Tikhonov regularization parameter that ensures a unique solution to the optimization problem.

sol_ir

(default is NULL) Isotonic regression solution used as the Tikhonov regularization center, allowing the optimization problem to be formulated as a projection. (If NULL, the solution is calculated within the optimization solver)

Value

A list containing the following elements:

x

Optimal solution satisfying the constraints.

blocks

Optimal partition of the solution satisfying the constraints.

nb_outer_loop

Number of outer iterations required to solve the optimization problem (OP).

nb_inner_loop

Number of inner iterations required to solve the optimization problem (OP).

converged

For loss = "smoothH", a logical vector indicating whether the optimization converged for each aggregated block. Its length equals the number of aggregated blocks. Otherwise, NULL.

kantorovich

For loss = "smoothH", a logical vector indicating whether the block solution satisfies the convergence criterion based on the Kantorovich method. Its length equals the number of aggregated blocks. Otherwise, NULL.

References

Wang, X., Ying, J., Cardoso, J. V. M., & Palomar, D. P. (2022, June). Efficient Algorithms for General Isotone Optimization. In Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (Vol. 36, No. 8, pp. 8575-8583).

Author

Xiwen Wang, Zé Vinícius, and Daniel P. Palomar

Examples

library(IsotoneOptimization)
set.seed(10)
solve_isotone_2d_grid(rnorm(10), rep(1,10))
#> $x
#>  [1] -0.6688162 -0.6688162 -0.6688162 -0.6688162 -0.3265023 -0.3265023
#>  [7] -0.6688162 -0.3265023 -0.3265023 -0.2564784
#> 
#> $blocks
#> $blocks[[1]]
#> [1] 1 2 3 4 7
#> 
#> $blocks[[2]]
#> [1] 5 6 8 9
#> 
#> $blocks[[3]]
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> 
#> $nb_outer_loop
#> [1] 7
#> 
#> $nb_inner_loop
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $converged
#> integer(0)
#> 
#> $kantorovich
#> logical(0)
#>
